executiveSummary: Multiple actively exploited edge-access vulnerabilities and campaign advisories elevate near-term risk for OT operators. Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway unauthenticated RCE is being exploited in the wild and is broadly deployed on critical infrastructure perimeters (immediate patching and compromise assessments are required). Security Advisory Supporting Advisory F5 BIG-IP APM OAuth Authorization Server configurations are under active exploitation for unauthenticated RCE; compromise can enable perimeter breach and potential pivot toward OT jump hosts and engineering assets. Security Advisory U.S. agencies warn of active threat activity against Siemens S7-series PLCs across Water/Wastewater, Energy, and Manufacturing sectors, highlighting AI-assisted discovery and unauthorized S7comm operations; immediate hardening and network isolation are advised. Security Advisory CISA's weekly vulnerability bulletin features multiple OT-adjacent, publicly exploitable issues-most notably Advantech WISE-6610 industrial gateways (remote command injection) and eProsima Fast-DDS flaws affecting industrial messaging-requiring rapid triage in utility and manufacturing environments. Security Bulletin Edge risk remains elevated: CISA and national CERTs confirm active exploitation of Citrix NetScaler and add further KEV items (Citrix, Fortinet FortiMail, Zammad), indicating continued targeting of remote access and ITSM platforms often adjacent to OT. CISA KEV CISA KEV SonicWall SMA1000 hotfixes address a CVSS 10.0 pre-auth SSRF in widely used remote access gateways; while exploitation is not yet reported for this set, prior similar flaws were abused this year. View Article Enterprise-to-OT pivot paths remain a priority. CISA's "Tale of Two SOCs" red-team findings at a water utility show containment at the IT/OT DMZ can hold even as cloud identities are abused-reinforcing the need for identity hygiene, cloud app governance, and OT egress controls. relevance: Today's risk posture is driven by concurrent, actively exploited edge-access vulnerabilities (Citrix NetScaler, F5 BIG-IP APM) combined with confirmatory federal advisories of direct PLC targeting. These align with common enterprise-to-OT intrusion patterns: initial edge compromise, identity abuse, and attempts to traverse OT DMZ jump hosts. In parallel, high-impact OT vendor advisories (Johnson Controls EasyIO FG EOL, Hitachi Energy REB500, Hitachi Asset Suite) and this week's CVE bulletins affecting industrial gateways and messaging stacks broaden the potential attack surface. Operators should prioritize edge patching, identity hardening, and stringent IT/OT segmentation with focused monitoring on PLC programming channels and engineering workstations.

descriptions: Edge exploitation and access broker tactics: unauthenticated RCE/DoS on NetScaler and BIG-IP; post-exploitation token/session hijacking; DTLS-focused probes.
PLC targeting: unauthorized S7comm interactions, snap7-based scripting, CPU enumeration, data block read/write; TCP/102 exposure abuse.
WAF bypass via encoding/canonicalization (PeopleSoft); traversal patterns using "::" to disclose Tomcat webapp configs (Atlassian CVE-2026-21589).
AD domain weaponization: malicious GPOs linked at domain root to propagate ransom notes/policy changes (no Windows encryptors required).
Supply-chain abuse: npm postinstall loaders (Overlord RAT); macOS LaunchAgent/Zsh/Git-hook persistence; CalDAV/HTTP PUT exfiltration.
DNS/PKI misuse: registry hijack → misissued DV TLS certs enabling potential regional MitM against public services.

outlook72h: Complete NetScaler and BIG-IP APM emergency patching and compromise assessments; revoke sessions/tokens and rotate VPN/AAA credentials. Block TCP/102 at all internet and IT/OT perimeters; validate no direct PLC exposure to the internet; baseline and alert on S7comm anomalies. Apply SonicWall SMA1000 hotfixes; shift admin interfaces behind VPN/allowlists; increase logging/egress monitoring on gateways. Triage bulletin-listed OT-adjacent CVEs (WISE-6610, Fast-DDS, AVEVA PIM) for exposure; implement virtual patching or isolation where updates require downtime. Harden identity: enforce MFA, reduce over-privileged cloud apps, enable continuous access evaluation and app consent governance.
